scope: Reviewed personal static-web release commands only, not general Expo/native/Atlas tooling safety. No exemption may apply to a bundled browser or Worker package.

uuid.assessment: xcode 3.0.1 lib/pbxProject.js generateUuid calls uuid.v4() without a buffer. jest-junit 16.0.0 utils/getOptions.js destructures v1 and calls it without a buffer for an XML filename. Neither invokes vulnerable v3/v5/v6 with caller-supplied buffers. These are the only installed direct consumers; all consumer/package source trees are pinned. Xcode is native configuration tooling, not a server API.

advisories.title: uuid: Missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6 when buf is provided

sharp.assessment: The only vulnerable copy is miniflare 4.20251105.0/node_modules/sharp 0.33.5. Its dist/src/index.js IMAGES_PLUGIN getBindings/getNodeBindings/getServices return empty when options.images is absent; imagesLocalFetcher dynamically imports sharp only for that binding. proof/runtime.mjs enables modules/D1 and a fixed mocked outbound verifier, not images. Production wrangler.jsonc has assets/D1 only. Real Wrangler 4.158.0 uses its separate miniflare 5 copy with sharp 0.35.5; root asset generation also uses sharp 0.35.5. Static assets are offloaded, never decoded by the production Worker. Enabling Images or changing these exact source/config trees requires a new review or compatible upgrade.

advisories.title: sharp inherited vulnerabilities in libvips: CVE-2026-33327, CVE-2026-33328, CVE-2026-35590, CVE-2026-35591
sharp: Vulnerabilities in libheif: GHSA-g89c-p67h-r497 and GHSA-2jg2-4ch7-h545
sharp : Vulnerability in librsvg dependency CVE-2026-96889

stream-json.assessment: The sole consumer is expo-atlas 0.4.3 build/src/utils/jsonl.js. It imports Disassembler and Stringer to serialize bundler-owned object data, not affected filters, JSONC parser/verifier or Assembler. parseJsonLine uses native JSON.parse on a local generated line. The personal export removes EXPO_ATLAS from its child environment and never serves the Atlas development UI. The general open-analyzer/generate-web-stats upstream scripts are outside this reviewed release boundary and must not be exposed to uploaded traces. Full Atlas and stream-json trees are pinned; any new import or consumer invalidates this assessment.

advisories.title: stream-json: pick/ignore/filter/replace filters are O(depth²) on nested input — small crafted JSON blocks the event loop for seconds→minutes (DoS)
stream-json: JSONC parser and verifier re-scan the whole accumulated comment on every input chunk
stream-json has a prototype pollution issue: Assembler writes this.current[this.key] on plain objects

deepmerge.assessment: All installed consumers are @expo/config 58.0.8 and 11.0.10 Config.js, and jest-config 30.5.2 build/index.js. They merge checked-in executable application/plugin config and Jest defaults/presets/globals, not feed/API/upload JSON. The vulnerable target-own __proto__ copy remains in deepmerge 4.3.1; this is not claimed patched. Release runs only reviewed static export/test configs from the exact candidate with frozen integrity-checked dependencies. Candidate jobs have read-only permissions and no deploy/write credentials. Native prebuild, arbitrary supplied presets and user config services are not an accepted release operation. Config/consumer/lock drift requires review.

advisories.title: deepmerge mergeObject() allows prototype poisoning of returned objects

glob.assessment: Full installed direct-consumer inventory includes Expo config/plugins/fingerprint/Metro/CLI, Jest config/runtime/reporters/test-exclude, Lingui, Babel module resolver, sucrase, Sentry build plugins, expo-updates and rimraf. Active export/test/catalog calls use local project/package globs, not remote patterns or a request timeout as a traversal security boundary. Babel normalizeRoot uses glob.sync on configured roots; Metro getWatchFolders searches package.json; Jest uses sync project/module/coverage paths; Lingui uses sync checked-in catalogs. Expo CLI utils/glob.js anyMatchAsync does have AbortController first-match cancellation, but no consumer imports/calls it in this exact installed CLI tree; it must not be treated as a safe timeout. Sentry upload paths are not invoked in the personal export. No hosted glob/native/dev service is deployed. All copies and every direct consumer tree plus release configs/lock are pinned, including unaffected glob 7. A new glob service, imported cancellation helper or changed patterns invalidates this bounded build assessment.

advisories.title: Glob: AbortSignal cancellation bypass allows post-timeout filesystem traversal

minimatch.assessment: Consumers are the fully inventoried glob copies, test-exclude, @expo/fingerprint, @ts-morph/common and ESLint configuration tooling. The release uses checked-in catalog/module/project/instrumentation patterns and package-owned fixed glob patterns, not network-supplied globparts. test-exclude matches filename against configured include/exclude; fingerprint Path.js builds matchers from local ignore patterns; ts-morph common uses minimatch for source-file patterns in lexicon generation. Lexicon source and build configs are versioned, not a public schema/pattern upload endpoint. Existing vulnerable amplification is not claimed fixed; release CI is a bounded read-only job and public requests cannot invoke this toolchain. Package/consumer/pattern/config/lock drift or runtime bundling fails closed; do not use this assessment for an untrusted build-as-a-service.

advisories.title: minimatch has potential denial of service via globparts amplification
